title: Translate jargon without changing the claim
goal: Make a technical statement understandable without inventing business impact.
explanation: Plain language should preserve uncertainty, conditions and numerical meaning. A model may replace jargon with impressive but unsupported savings or risk claims. Use a short fictional source and demand a parallel evidence ledger so the reader can see what was simplified and what remains unknown.
sampleInput: Source: “The prototype caches repeated requests for five minutes. In a 100-request test, 60 were served from cache. The test did not measure financial savings or peak-load behaviour.”
prompt: Rewrite the source for a non-technical operations reader. Preserve the five-minute window, the 60/100 test result and the unmeasured limits. Then provide a source-to-rewrite mapping. Do not convert cache hits into a claimed 60% cost reduction or a performance guarantee.
workedExample: Acceptable: “For five minutes, the prototype can reuse some recent answers. In one small test it reused stored results for 60 of 100 requests. We have not tested cost savings or heavy traffic.” A 60% savings claim is unsupported.

steps.title: Mark protected meaning
steps.text: Underline numbers, qualifiers and limitations in the source.

steps.title: Generate the rewrite
steps.text: Specify a reader and a shorter vocabulary, not a more persuasive sales message.

steps.title: Build a mapping
steps.text: Trace each rewritten claim to an exact source sentence.

steps.title: Challenge an overclaim
steps.text: Ask whether “60% cheaper” follows. Record why the missing cost measurements prevent that conclusion.

steps.title: User-test comprehension
steps.text: Ask a reader to explain what was measured and what was not.

checks: All source numbers and limitations survive the rewrite.
Cache-hit rate is not misrepresented as cost saving or guaranteed speed.
A reader can distinguish the measured result from the untested business effect.
commonMistakes: Replacing technical jargon with invented business metrics.
Deleting uncertainty because it makes the sentence shorter.
offline: Write a plain-language version yourself and highlight each source-to-rewrite link.
reflection: Which qualifier would most change a decision if it disappeared?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All source numbers and limitations survive the rewrite.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Cache-hit rate is not misrepresented as cost saving or guaranteed speed.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Replacing technical jargon with invented business metrics.
